newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian stocks fall but turnaround seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian stocks fall but turnaround seen soon.

text.p: Slovenian shares slipped on Tuesday, continuing to correct after steep rises over the past three weeks, but traders said they were confident the market could resume its upward trend later in the week.
"It was mostly domestic investors who were selling today, trying to realise their short-term profits," said Robert Rudolf, a trader at brokerage Moja delnica.
The seven-share SBI index fell 15.33 points or 1.21 percent to 1,254.60. Overall, five shares fell, nine rose and one was steady, while another nine were untraded.
"Compared to recent big jumps these declines over the past two days are very small," said Milos Pavlic, a trader at brokerage ABH.
Turnover fell to 464.3 million tolars from 591.6 million.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, firming 1.41 percent to 41,580 tolars on volume of 4,477 shares.
Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, falling 4.88 percent to 7,800 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
Preferred shares of bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice were the biggest gainer, firming 4.21 percent to 3,740 tolars on volume of 135 shares. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
